clue.text: No chicken-hearted description of Hamlet senior's death

definitions.text: No chicken-hearted description of Hamlet senior's death

parts.words: No chicken-hearted description of Hamlet senior's death
parts.note: the Ghost's phrase for his killing in Hamlet, with a pun on 'fowl': no chicken in it, just foulness

explanation.surface: A literary query about how the Ghost in Hamlet would describe his own killing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ghost in Shakespeare's play uses exactly this phrase for his brother's crime against him.

clue.text: Post-impressionist shrouded in sea mist?

indicators.note: letters wrapped up and muffled in fog suggest them being jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter disappears into the fog over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrouded in' signals rearranging SEAMIST into the painter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse, the French painter, is usually grouped with the post-impressionist and Fauvist generation.

clue.text: Moving back in the fight

parts.note: a retreating army's defensive engagement, read as literally moving backwards in battle

explanation.surface: A soldier edging away mid-battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard engagement is fought by troops covering a retreat from the enemy.

clue.text: Spotted, I'd say

indicators.note: an invitation to pronounce the clue word rather than read its spelling

parts.note: the contraction of I would, sounding like the past of a verb meaning looked at

explanation.surface: Someone claiming they noticed something first.
explanation.definitionFit: To have spotted something is to have looked at or seen it.

clue.text: How to expect a worldly inheritance from the Bible

definitions.text: How to expect a worldly inheritance from the Bible

parts.words: How to expect a worldly inheritance from the Bible
parts.note: alludes to the Beatitude promising that the humble shall inherit the earth

explanation.surface: Advice on scriptural terms for receiving an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sermon on the Mount says the gentle and humble will inherit the earth, so humility is the manner prescribed.

clue.text: Quick fire picture

definitions.meaning: a hurried shot taken without careful aim

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hasty unaimed gunshot and an informal photograph taken quickly.

clue.text: State in which Dad takes cover, conceivably

parts.note: a familiar word for a male parent
a hood is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A joke about the condition a father enters by having children, with conception punned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' simply joins the parts; 'conceivably' is a playful nod to how one becomes a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a parent who is male is a condition or status one is in.

clue.text: Inexpert work force in the party?

definitions.text: Inexpert work force in the party?

parts.words: Inexpert work force in the party?
parts.note: workers without training, with a teasing hint at Britain's Labour Party

explanation.surface: A dig at a political party's membership as untrained workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers without trained skills make up an untrained workforce.

clue.text: Contemplates ways, so to speak

indicators.note: tells us to treat the preceding word as spoken rather than written

parts.note: methods or routes, said out loud

explanation.surface: Someone thinking over different methods.
explanation.definitionFit: To contemplate options is to ponder or consider them, assessing their merits.

clue.text: Alias the swinging barman

parts.note: a pub worker who swings is really an acrobat who works on a swinging bar

explanation.surface: A nickname for a lively bartender.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer on a swinging bar is literally a man of the bar who swings.

clue.text: See 9
Second period plant

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A botanist describing a later era of plant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is an aromatic herb, so a type of plant.

clue.text: Overdoing it with a heavy coat

definitions.text: Overdoing it with a heavy coat

parts.words: Overdoing it with a heavy coat
parts.note: slapping on a thick layer, as a builder does to walls, or laying it on thick

explanation.surface: Someone overdressed in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a thick layer of render to a wall is this job; it also means daubing something heavily.

clue.text: Game at worst barely tolerated

parts.note: a card game in which losing leaves players nearly naked, a pun on barely

explanation.surface: A sport that is only just accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game where losers shed clothing, so at worst one ends up bare.

clue.text: Takes from a book of the Bible

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex-works
Acts of the Apostles is a New Testament book

explanation.surface: Someone quoting from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment is to demand and take it.

clue.text: Loops the loop, finding hazards in the way

definitions.text: Loops the loop, finding hazards in the way

parts.words: Loops the loop, finding hazards in the way
parts.note: an aerobatic picture hiding road dangers; a hole is a loop-like gap

explanation.surface: A stunt pilot meeting obstacles mid-manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Holes worn in a road surface are hazards to drivers on their way.

clue.text: Enter USA in style for a drink

indicators.note: style suggests the letters being given a new fashion or arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to arrive in America elegantly for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white French wine from Bordeaux, here in its anglicised spelling.

clue.text: Crazy gear Jolson donned for a song

parts.note: mad means crazy
a rig is equipment or outfit
Al Jolson, the American singer

explanation.surface: A singer putting on wild clothes to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Fashionable pretty female doctor?

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stylish and in vogue is in fashion.

clue.text: Burdened with wealth, maybe

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both carrying a heavy load and, informally, being very rich.

clue.text: Lodge in a ready-made position

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Moving into a house already prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'ready-made' and 'position'; 'in' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge money or a document is to put it somewhere for safekeeping, a synonym.

clue.text: Cuts back to firm a form of 12

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the preceding word round

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm trimming costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CUTS into STUC; 12 is PLASTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine render applied to walls, a kind of plasterwork.

clue.text: Cut meaning the chop for someone

definitions.text: Cut meaning the chop for someone

parts.words: Cut meaning the chop for someone
parts.note: a cut that leaves someone headless, the chop taken literally

explanation.surface: Being fired from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead someone is to cut off the head.

clue.text: Find fault with the fish

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to complain pettily and a common freshwater fish.

clue.text: Claim I put out for shellfish

indicators.note: put out says the named letter is removed from the word

explanation.surface: Someone claiming to have discarded shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes the I from CLAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve mollusc.

clue.text: Sly guy in a shiny raincoat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a smooth trickster and a glossy waterproof coat.

clue.text: Hard on the feet, we hear

indicators.note: signals that a word is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: hard skin found on the feet

explanation.surface: Someone tough walking hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfeeling person is hard-hearted.

clue.text: Accepted for high distinction on a rotatory basis?

definitions.text: Accepted for high distinction on a rotatory basis?

parts.words: Accepted for high distinction on a rotatory basis?
parts.note: ranked by achievement, with rotatory hinting at an order of knighthood or merit

explanation.surface: Honours handed out in rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranking people by achievement means arranging them by how good they are.
